facts.claim: Savitri was a princess who chose her own husband rather than having one arranged for her.

sources.quote: Surely it was on this very business that she had been sent, and she returneth now (from her search).

facts.claim: The sage Narada warned that Satyavan had exactly one defect: he would die within a year.

sources.quote: He hath one only defect that hath overwhelmed all his virtues.
Within a year from this day, Satyavan, endued with a short life will cast off his body!

facts.claim: Told to pick another husband, Savitri refused, saying she would only choose once.

sources.quote: Indeed, with a life short or long, possessed of virtues or bereft of them, I have, for once, selected my husband. Twice I shall not select.

facts.claim: Savitri married Satyavan in the forest hermitage and lived there as an ascetic, but she counted the days to his foretold death.

sources.quote: But the words spoken by Narada were present night and day in the mind of the sorrowful Savitri.

facts.claim: On the predicted day, Satyavan went into the forest to cut wood, and Savitri insisted on going with him.

sources.quote: It behoveth thee not to go alone! I will accompany thee. I cannot bear to be separated from thee!

facts.claim: Satyavan grew weak and laid his head in Savitri's lap, and then Yama himself appeared, dressed in red, carrying a noose.

sources.quote: The next moment she saw a person clad in red attire with his head decked with a diadem.
And he was of a darkish hue, had red eyes, carried a noose in his hand, and was dreadful to behold.

facts.claim: Savitri asked Yama why he had come in person instead of sending his usual messengers.

sources.quote: I had heard that thy emissaries come to take away mortals, O worshipful one! Why then, O lord, hast thou come in person?

facts.claim: Yama pulled Satyavan's soul from his body and headed south; Savitri followed him on foot.

sources.quote: And binding Satyavan's vital essence, Yama proceeded in a southerly direction.
began to follow Yama

facts.claim: Yama told her to turn back, and she refused, arguing that walking seven steps with someone creates a friendship.

sources.quote: Desist, O Savitri! Go back, and perform the funeral obsequies of thy lord!
by walking only seven paces with another, one contracteth a friendship with one's companion

facts.claim: Pleased with her reasoning, Yama offered her any boon except her husband's life — and she asked for her blind father-in-law's sight.

sources.quote: Except the life of thy husband, O thou of faultless features, I will bestow on thee any boon that thou mayst solicit!
Let that king through thy favour attain his eye-sight, and become strong 'like either fire or the Sun!

facts.claim: Her second boon was that her father-in-law regain his lost kingdom.

sources.quote: May that monarch regain his kingdom. And may that superior of mine never renounce his duties!

facts.claim: Her third boon was a hundred sons for her own father, to continue his line.

sources.quote: That he may have a hundred sons begotten of his loins, so that his line may be perpetuated, is the third boon I would ask of thee!

facts.claim: Her fourth boon was a hundred sons born to herself and Satyavan — granted while Satyavan was still dead.

sources.quote: Both of me and Satyavan's loins, begotten by both of us, let there be a century of sons possessed of strength and prowess and capable of perpetuating our race!

facts.claim: The loophole: she pointed out that the promised sons could not exist without their father, so Yama's own boon required Satyavan to live.

sources.quote: the boon thou hast already given me is incapable of accomplishment without union with my husband
I ask for this boon, 'May Satyavan be restored to life, for by that thy words will be made true.'

facts.claim: Yama conceded, untied his noose, and granted Satyavan a life of four hundred years.

sources.quote: Vivaswat's son, Yama, the dispenser of justice, untied his noose
And along with thee, he will attain a life of four hundred years.

facts.claim: Satyavan woke on her lap, thinking he had merely slept long, and asked where the dark figure had gone.

sources.quote: Alas, I have slept long! Wherefore didst thou not awake me? And where is that same sable person that was dragging me away?

facts.claim: Savitri later told the assembled sages that she won five boons from Yama by praising him with truthful words.

sources.quote: Thereupon I began to praise that august god, with truthful words. And he granted me five boons, of do ye hear from me!
